stem: In this excerpt, the authors of the Virginia Declaration of Rights are describing rights they consider —

options.label: F
options.text: granted to citizens by their government

visual_elements: That all Men are . . . equally free & independent, & have certain . . . Rights, of which they can not by any Compact, deprive or divest [remove] their Posterity [future generations]; among which are the Enjoyment of Life and Liberty, with the Means of acquiring and possessing Property, and pursuing and obtaining Happiness and Safety. —Virginia Declaration of Rights, 1776
